title: Design a Distributed Computer-Use & Browser Agent Execution Platform
prompt: Design a multi-tenant Computer-Use & Browser Agent execution platform sustaining 10,000 concurrent browser sessions, < 150 ms warm-sandbox allocation, live WebRTC/VNC user takeover, indirect prompt-injection defense, and full step-by-step replay traces.

spark.summary: Combine a Temporal durable session orchestrator with a pre-warmed Firecracker/Playwright microVM pool, an egress-filtering proxy, perceptual-hash screenshot deduplication, and an immutable replay ledger.
spark.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, pre-warm Firecracker memory snapshots with Chromium booted so tenant sessions attach in < 150 ms while keeping strict per-session KVM isolation.
spark.byteSummary:
Booting a fresh Linux VM and Chromium binary cold takes 2–4 seconds, blowing the < 150 ms interactive allocation budget. Maintaining a **Pre-Warmed Firecracker Snapshot Pool** restores identical clean Chromium memory images in < 125 ms, binding each session via `AF_VSOCK` to a Temporal worker.

Each step compresses screenshots via perceptual-hash delta checks (skipping redundant VLM calls when the screen hasn't changed), streams live WebRTC/VNC frames so users can take over CAPTCHAs or logins, and routes all outbound browser traffic through an egress proxy blocking RFC-1918/metadata IPs.

Every screenshot, DOM snapshot, and action is archived to S3/Iceberg for deterministic debugging and compliance replay.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Distributed Computer-Use & Browser Agent Execution Platform without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, pre-warm Firecracker memory snapshots with Chromium booted so tenant sessions attach in < 150 ms while keeping strict per-session KVM isolation.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
